**Publish gate report: search ad**

**Going out:** Google-style search ad, headline "Tea Subscription UK", UK audience.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Monthly loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right." | **Unproven.** It's an implied satisfaction guarantee/remedy promise. The policy says we have no such offer (section 3: "you'll love it or it's free" is not an offer). Nothing in section 2 backs a remedy promise. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | On policy list (shipping policy). Fine. |

**Regulated claims:** Touches prices/offers. The delivery threshold matches the policy exactly, so no problem. The "make it right" line is the only risk, since it promises a remedy we haven't defined.

**House style:** Reads plain and warm, no banned words, no AI tells. "Tea Subscription UK" is a keyword-style headline, which is normal for search. Fine.

**Disclosure:** Our own paid ad; the platform marks it. No extra label needed.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite):**
Description: "Monthly loose leaf tea. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25."
This swaps the vague promise for a claim that's on the policy list ("Subscribers can pause or cancel any time").

**Needs a decision:**
- If Sam wants to keep a "we'll make it right" promise, the actual returns/refund terms need to be written into the policy first. My suggestion is to use the pause/cancel line instead.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). Approval needed for the revised copy, not this draft. Not published, and no approval has been recorded.
